title: Make your pet the narrator
description: Turn a pet portrait and a short voice track into a talking-animal concept.
inputs: A clear pet portrait and an audio clip you own.
steps: Choose a front-facing portrait.
Record an original short voiceover.
Generate with the provider and review the mouth movement.
prompt: Create a warm, playful talking-pet clip using my reference photo and original voiceover. Preserve the pet’s markings. Keep movements subtle. Do not add people or logos.
caution: Photo consent and voice rights matter. Animal lip sync can fail.

title: Give your pet a dance-floor moment
description: Explore a photo-to-dance template without writing a long technical prompt.
evidence: Provider publishes pet and human dance templates.
inputs: One pet photo; some templates require two.
steps: Browse the live template library.
Check required photos, credit cost and music terms.
Generate and review anatomy before sharing.
prompt: Design an original short pet dance concept from my photo. Use a gentle bounce, recognizable fur markings and a fixed camera. Use original or properly licensed audio.
caution: Template availability, music rights and provider charges vary.

title: Remix a character’s movement
description: Use character-motion tools for an original meme or performance concept.
evidence: Official platform provides motion-focused AI creation.
inputs: A character image and a movement concept.
steps: Explore the provider’s creation tools.
Use a character image you have permission to animate.
Test one short motion and inspect the output.
prompt: Help me storyboard an original 6-second character-motion remix. Explain the input assets I need and suggest a simple movement that avoids complex occlusion.
caution: Check likeness consent and the rights to any reference performance.

title: Bring a product photo to life
description: Plan a short product reveal from a single clean reference image.
inputs: A product image and a simple shot idea.
steps: Prepare a clean product image.
Describe one camera move and one product action.
Generate externally and check logos and shape.
prompt: Create a short product reveal from this image. Keep packaging, logo and proportions unchanged. Use soft studio light and a slow camera orbit. No additional text.
caution: Small text, logos and product geometry may change during generation.

title: Try a nostalgic yearbook portrait
description: Explore portrait styles and build a specific creative brief before spending credits.
evidence: Official product offers AI image and video generation.
inputs: Portrait references accepted by the provider.
steps: Check the provider’s current photo requirements.
Choose era, lighting and wardrobe cues.
Review face consistency and download terms.
prompt: Create a 1990s school-portrait concept: soft studio flash, a blue mottled backdrop and restrained film grain. Preserve identity and natural skin texture. No school logo.
caution: This is a style idea, not a verified template or guaranteed likeness result.

title: Turn an idea into a social design
description: Build a visual concept, then refine layout and readable copy in a design editor.
evidence: Official page describes AI design and creative tools.
inputs: A topic, audience and desired format.
steps: Describe the audience and main message.
Ask for one visual direction and short headline.
Edit typography and verify export rights.
prompt: Design a square social post for [audience] about [topic]. Use one clear headline, generous negative space and a simple visual hierarchy. Provide three concise copy options.
caution: Review generated text, stock licensing and brand accuracy.

title: Edit a video through its transcript
description: Use transcript-led editing to tighten a spoken video and create a clearer story.
evidence: Official product describes text-based video and audio editing.
inputs: A recorded video or audio file.
steps: Import a recording you own.
Review the transcript for errors.
Make a short edit and inspect timing and captions.
prompt: Review this transcript for repetition, long pauses and unclear explanations. Suggest a tighter edit while preserving the speaker’s meaning. Do not invent quotes.
caution: Transcription accuracy varies; check names and caption timing.

title: Find an automation starting point
description: Search community workflows and adapt one to your own apps and data.
evidence: Official library lists workflow automation templates.
inputs: A repeated task and access to the required apps.
steps: Describe the trigger and desired result.
Inspect a template’s integrations and code.
Test with sample data before using live accounts.
prompt: Design a workflow for [task]. Specify trigger, input schema, validation, actions and failure handling. Prepare drafts for external messages rather than sending automatically.
caution: Templates are not audited here. Hosting and model/API usage may cost money.

title: Connect a simple workflow visually
description: Map a trigger, transformation and destination before building a larger process.
inputs: Two apps and a clearly defined recurring task.
steps: Choose a small task with observable output.
Inspect the template and connection requirements.
Run sample records and check failures and duplicates.
prompt: Map [task] as trigger → validation → transformation → destination. Include duplicate protection and an error notification. List the permissions each app needs.
caution: App permissions, operation allowances and third-party fees differ.

title: Start with a prebuilt app connection
description: Use a template to connect tools, then inspect the exact actions before activation.
inputs: A trigger app and a destination app.
steps: Search templates for your two apps.
Check each action and its account access.
Test a sample and enable only the approved actions.
prompt: Help me plan an automation between [app A] and [app B]. Identify the trigger, field mapping, missing-data behavior and duplicate handling. Show the test plan before activation.
caution: A template is not proof of reliability for your data or accounts.
